name: שָׂרָף
summary: A man of Judah, of the sons of Shelah son of Judah, named with Jokim, the men of Cozeba and Joash, “who ruled in Moab”, in a record the Chronicler calls ancient (1Ch 4:21–22). The name is spelled as the noun שָׂרָף, “burning one”, the word for the burning serpent of the wilderness (Num 21:6, 8); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, וְשָׂרָף, who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem; and the records are ancient.”
“The sons of Shelah son of Judah”, at the head of the list.
The noun שָׂרָף “burning (serpent)”, the name's spelling.

note: Takes u.cj.ad; the database also counts Isa 30:6 under this key by spelling, which is the serpent, not the man. Whether the name is the serpent word or a participle-like “burning one” the text does not show.
